algorithms.name: Conformal Predictive Programming (CPP-MIP / CPP-KKT, plus robust-KL CPP and the SA/SAA solvers in the same repo)
algorithms.reference: Y. Zhao, X. Yu, J. V. Deshmukh, L. Lindemann (later arXiv versions add M. Sesia), 'Conformal Predictive Programming for Chance Constrained Optimization', arXiv:2402.07407, 2024. Journal/conference venue: unverified.
algorithms.core_idea: Takes a chance-constrained problem min J(x) s.t. P(f(x,Y)<=0)>=1-delta and replaces the probability with the conformal quantile lemma over K samples of Y. The quantile is encoded as an MILP (CPP-MIP) or as an LP with KKT conditions (CPP-KKT). Joint chance constraints are handled with 'Max' (one max-score) or 'Union' (Bonferroni). A robust version covers a KL-divergence distribution shift. The repo's solve() also implements the scenario approach ('SA') and sample average approximation ('SAA') behind the same interface.
algorithms.how_to_adapt_to_our_problem: Decision vector: per-pass margins m in R^K (h_k = w/2 - m_k), or, to keep the dimension low and the result transferable, per-slope-bin margins m_b with b=1..B (B=4-8 DEM side-slope bins) plus two boundary margins. Pass positions are a deterministic linear map of m: y_1 = y_lo + h_1, y_{k+1} = y_k + h_k + h_{k+1}. Add this as hs/gs constraints, plus y_K + h_K >= y_hi. The random parameter Y^(i) is the executed offset profile set {e_k^(i)(x)} from calibration run i on the reference plan (core.simulate). Chance constraint, using joint_method='Max': f(m,Y) = max( max_k max_x [e_{k+1}(x)-e_k(x) - m_k - m_{k+1}], boundary terms e_1 - m_1 and -(e_K) - m_K against the main-area edges ). This is linear in m, so CPP-MIP is an exact small MILP: n_cal=100 binaries and K<=100 continuous variables (CVXPY with HiGHS or Gurobi). Objective J(m) = sum_k m_k, i.e. total overlap. Fix K and scan K in {K_CE-2, ..., K_CE}, keeping the smallest feasible K. To handle decision dependence fairly, wrap it in the same fixed-point loop as calibrate_conformal: re-simulate at the CPP plan, re-solve, 3 iterations. Run four variants: (a) CPP-MIP on all calibration data; (b) CPP-split, which optimizes the shape of m on half the data and then conformally calibrates one scalar multiplier on the other half; (c) joint_method='Union' to mirror CE-pair; (d) robust=True with a KL radius estimated between blocks/days for the CitrusFarm leave-one-out splits. Expected result: (a) gives lower overlap than CE-U but falls below 0.9 on test because K free margins are fitted on 100 samples, while (b) is valid. That is the scientific argument for why CE fixes a 1-D family a priori. Plug the result into exp_main through sig_fn = interpolated m(y) with lam=1.
algorithms.open_source_code: https://github.com/SAIDS-Lab/Conformal-Predictive-Programming-for-CCO (resources/solver.py: solve(x_dim, delta, training_Ys, hs, gs, f, J, method in {SA, SAA, CPP-KKT, CPP-MIP}, robust, epsilon, joint_method in {Union, Max}))

algorithms.name: Probabilistic coverage under pose uncertainty / belief-space coverage planning (Paull et al.; Schirmer et al.)
algorithms.reference: L. Paull, M. Seto, H. Li, 'Area coverage planning that accounts for pose uncertainty with an AUV seabed surveying application', ICRA 2014, pp. 6592-6599, DOI 10.1109/ICRA.2014.6907832. L. Paull, M. Seto, J. J. Leonard, H. Li, 'Probabilistic cooperative mobile robot area coverage and its application to autonomous seabed mapping', IJRR 37(1):21-45, 2018. R. Schirmer, P. Biber, C. Stachniss, 'Coverage Path Planning in Belief Space', ICRA 2019 (pages unverified).
algorithms.category: coverage path planning under localization uncertainty (model-based Gaussian belief)
algorithms.core_idea: Paull: map the robot's pose-estimate distribution through the sensor/footprint model to get a probability-of-coverage map over a discretized workspace, then choose coverage paths adaptively by entropy reduction until every cell is covered with high probability. Schirmer: predict the belief (pose covariance) along candidate parallel-lane (meander) coverage paths from a localizability prior plus odometry drift, then choose the lane pattern that is safest given the expected localization accuracy.
algorithms.how_to_adapt_to_our_problem: This is the coverage-domain, model-based competitor. (1) Belief model: linearize the closed-loop lateral dynamics already in core.simulate. States are [d, psi, int d] under the LQR-I gains from core._lqr_gains. Process noise: OU slip at nominal soil parameters (k_s and rough at mean moisture). Measurement noise: a Gaussian fit to the i2Nav RTK series. The DEM side slope enters as a known mean bias (-k_s*0.35*g_v*v). Propagate the steady-state lateral covariance P_k(x) and mean mu_k(x) along each candidate pass with a discrete Lyapunov/Kalman recursion. (2) Probability-of-coverage map on a 0.1 m grid of the main area: p_c(x,y) = 1 - prod_k [1 - P(|y - y_k - mu_k(x)| <= w/2)] under Gaussian beliefs. (3) Planner, Paull-style greedy/entropy: place pass k+1 at the largest y_{k+1} such that every cell between passes k and k+1 has p_c >= 1-eps_cell. Use two settings: eps_cell = eps (pointwise, as published) and eps_cell = eps/N_cells,eff (run-level via Bonferroni over decorrelation-length segments). (4) Optional Schirmer-style step: choose the driving angle theta from a set of candidate headings to minimize predicted uncertainty-weighted overlap. Evaluate with core.evaluate on the same test runs. Expected result: miscalibrated under heavy-tailed RTK and run-correlated slip gain (pointwise version far below 0.9, Bonferroni version conservative). This separates 'model-based belief' from 'data-calibrated' certification. No official code found; implement in numpy/scipy (about 150 lines).

algorithms.name: GP-based cautious tube / learning-based margin (Cautious GP-MPC; LB-NMPC path tracking; SafeMPC)
algorithms.reference: L. Hewing, J. Kabzan, M. N. Zeilinger, 'Cautious Model Predictive Control Using Gaussian Process Regression', IEEE TCST 28(6), 2020 (pages unverified; arXiv:1705.10702). C. J. Ostafew, A. P. Schoellig, T. D. Barfoot, 'Robust constrained learning-based NMPC enabling reliable mobile robot path tracking', IJRR 35(13):1547-1563, 2016. T. Koller, F. Berkenkamp, M. Turchetta, A. Krause, 'Learning-based Model Predictive Control for Safe Exploration', CDC 2018 (arXiv:1803.08287). Tooling: A. Lahr et al., 'L4acados', arXiv:2411.19258.
algorithms.category: Gaussian-process uncertainty tubes / learned constraint tightening
algorithms.core_idea: Learn the residual disturbance (here: lateral tracking error) with a GP as a function of state and terrain features. Use the GP mean as feedforward compensation and the GP predictive variance to tighten constraints through Gaussian chance constraints, i.e. a probabilistic tube of width z*sigma_GP. Ostafew et al. apply this to lateral path-error constraints for off-road path tracking, learning the disturbance from previous traversals.
algorithms.how_to_adapt_to_our_problem: Training data: executed runs on the TRAINING fields (the same split CE-A's sigma model and the cross-field learning baselines use). Samples are (features -> lateral offset e_k(x)), subsampled to about 20k points. Features: local DEM side slope g_y at (x, y_k), travel direction sign, slope-times-direction, along-track distance from line start (acquisition transient), controller id. Model: sparse heteroscedastic GP (GPyTorch SVGP, or sklearn GPR with RBF + WhiteKernel on a subsample). Planner: (a) mean compensation, shifting the reference line of pass k by -mu_GP to cancel predicted downhill slip (the LB-NMPC learned-disturbance idea); (b) tube erosion m_k = max_x z * sqrt(sig_k(x)^2 + sig_{k+1}(x)^2 + 2*cov_GP). Run two settings: z = Phi^-1(1-eps), the per-constraint cautious-MPC style, and z = Phi^-1(1-eps/(K+1)), Bonferroni across pairs. Then core.plan with sig_fn = m(y), lam=1. Also run 'CE-GP': use sigma_GP(y) as the sigma model inside CE-A (calibrate_conformal). This shows whether a learned heteroscedastic sigma finally gives CE-A a gain over CE-U where the DEM-slope sigma did not, and that CE can certify any learner. Expected: GP-cautious is either invalid (Gaussian tails versus heavy-tailed RTK) or conservative (Bonferroni), and CE-GP is valid and possibly tighter.
algorithms.open_source_code: https://github.com/befelix/safe-exploration (SafeMPC, GPy/PyTorch) ; https://github.com/IntelligentControlSystems/l4acados (GP-MPC in acados) ; implement GP with GPyTorch/sklearn

algorithms.name: Online receding-horizon conformal planning (adaptive CP / conformal MPC), adapted to pass-by-pass feedback replanning
algorithms.reference: A. Dixit, L. Lindemann, S. X. Wei, M. Cleaveland, G. J. Pappas, J. W. Burdick, 'Adaptive Conformal Prediction for Motion Planning among Dynamic Agents', L4DC 2023, PMLR 211:300-314 (arXiv:2212.00278). L. Lindemann, M. Cleaveland, G. Shim, G. J. Pappas, 'Safe Planning in Dynamic Environments using Conformal Prediction', IEEE RA-L 8(8), 2023 (arXiv:2210.10254). C. Stamouli, L. Lindemann, G. J. Pappas, 'Recursively Feasible Shrinking-Horizon MPC in Dynamic Environments with Conformal Prediction Guarantees', L4DC 2024, PMLR 242:1330-1342.
algorithms.core_idea: Lindemann et al.: CP regions on prediction errors of uncertain quantities, union-bounded over the horizon, enter an MPC as tightened constraints. Dixit et al.: the miscoverage level alpha_t is adapted online (ACI) from delayed observations so validity survives distribution shift. Stamouli et al.: relax constraints to the least restrictive available CP region to keep recursive feasibility.
algorithms.how_to_adapt_to_our_problem: This is the strongest practical competitor: it uses the RECORDED executed track of pass k, which a real RTK tractor logs, to place pass k+1. Then only the bound on the next pass's deviation e_{k+1} is needed, not the pass-to-pass difference. Implementation: add core.simulate_sequential(field, cond, rng, policy) that simulates one pass at a time, vectorized over R runs with per-run positions ys of shape (R, K). Policy: y_{k+1} = min_x [measured_edge_k(x)] + w/2 - q_t * sigma_{k+1}, where measured_edge_k = y_k + e_k_meas(x) + w/2 (measured including RTK noise). q_t is the CP quantile of one-pass deviation scores sup_x(-e_{k+1}(x))/sigma_{k+1} at level eps/(K+1) (Lindemann union bound), or ACI-adapted with alpha_{t+1} = alpha_t + gamma(eps/(K+1) - err_t), updated after every executed pass (Dixit). Use Stamouli's relaxation rule when the chord or headland makes the constraint infeasible. Metrics are unchanged (core.evaluate on the realized per-run ys). Also report the CE result as an 'offline CE + online ACI' hybrid, so the paper either shows CE's offline certificate is competitive or adopts the online variant as an extension. Without this, reviewers will ask why feedback from the logged previous pass is ignored.
algorithms.open_source_code: none found (no official repo surfaced for Lindemann 2023, Dixit 2023 or Stamouli 2024)

algorithms.name: IRIS-U^2: inspection/coverage planning under execution uncertainty with Monte-Carlo coverage-probability estimates
algorithms.reference: S. D. Alpert, K. Solovey, I. Klein, O. Salzman, 'Inspection Planning Under Execution Uncertainty', IEEE Transactions on Robotics 41:2406-2423, 2025 (arXiv:2309.06113).
algorithms.category: coverage/inspection planning under execution (localization) uncertainty, simulation-based chance constraints
algorithms.core_idea: Extends the A*-based IRIS inspection planner. Localization/execution uncertainty is turned into per-point-of-interest coverage probabilities by Monte-Carlo sampling of executions. The planner maximizes expected coverage subject to a bound on expected collision probability, minimizing length among ties. It reports confidence intervals that tighten with more MC samples.
algorithms.how_to_adapt_to_our_problem: This is the 'model-based Monte-Carlo planner' competitor; the coverage task name matches ours ('execution uncertainty'). Plan space: graph over (driving angle theta in 0-180 deg at 5 deg steps) x (erosion lam on a grid), or per-pass increments searched best-first. For each candidate plan, run M=200 MC rollouts of the planner's INTERNAL execution model and estimate P(no miss) with a Clopper-Pearson lower bound (and expected missed area, path length, passes). The internal model is core.simulate with nominal soil parameters and a Gaussian RTK model, i.e. no access to the real heavy-tailed RTK series or the test-time moisture distribution. Choose the shortest-path plan whose lower bound is >= 1-eps. Evaluate on the TRUE test simulator/RTK replay like every other method. Also run an 'oracle' variant whose internal model equals the test model: it gives an efficiency frontier line for the plots (best achievable overlap at P=0.9). Expected: the nominal-model version is miscalibrated (optimistic), the oracle is tight but needs the true model, and CE gets near-oracle overlap with only 100 calibration runs and no model. Runtime matters: report CPU time per field, since MC-in-the-loop is costly.

algorithms.name: Full-vector scenario optimization with sampling-and-discarding / wait-and-judge a-posteriori certificate
algorithms.reference: M. C. Campi, S. Garatti, 'Wait-and-judge scenario optimization', Mathematical Programming 167:155-189, 2018 (DOI 10.1007/s10107-016-1056-9). Non-convex extension: S. Garatti, M. C. Campi, 'Non-convex scenario optimization', Mathematical Programming, 2025. Sampling-and-discarding (Campi & Garatti, JOTA 2011) is already cited in exp_lib.scenario_lambda; venue not re-verified in this sweep.
algorithms.core_idea: Solve the sampled robust program over all decision variables, then certify the risk a posteriori from the number of support scenarios s* actually observed (wait-and-judge), rather than from the dimension d. Sampling-and-discarding removes k samples to reduce conservatism while keeping a PAC (1-beta) guarantee.
algorithms.how_to_adapt_to_our_problem: The current 'Scenario (Campi-Garatti)' baseline is a scalar lambda rule (d=1) on the CE score, which is a category, not the algorithm as used in planning. The proper competitor optimizes the full per-pass margin vector m in R^K (or per-slope-bin m_b): min sum_k m_k s.t. e_{k+1}^(i)(x) - e_k^(i)(x) <= m_k + m_{k+1} for all i, k, x, plus boundary constraints. This is an LP, solvable with the CPP repo's 'SA' method or with scipy.optimize.linprog. Then (a) a-priori guarantee with d=K, and report the number of calibration runs required (about 2(K+ln(1/beta))/eps, i.e. 1000-2000 runs for K=50-100, versus 100 for CE); (b) a-posteriori wait-and-judge certificate from the observed s*; (c) greedy discarding of k scenarios. Same fixed-point re-simulation for decision dependence. Expected: overlap is competitive or lower, but at n=100 the certificate is weak or vacuous, or it needs about 10x more runs. Plot 'certified risk vs number of calibration runs' alongside CE.

algorithms.name: Conformal Decision Theory (conformal controller for online risk control of a decision parameter)
algorithms.reference: J. Lekeufack, A. N. Angelopoulos, A. Bajcsy, M. I. Jordan, J. Malik, 'Conformal Decision Theory: Safe Autonomous Decisions from Imperfect Predictions', ICRA 2024 (arXiv:2310.05921).
algorithms.category: online conformal risk control of decisions
algorithms.core_idea: Given a family of decision rules D^lambda, the conformal controller updates lambda_t online from the observed loss, lambda_{t+1} = lambda_t + eta (L_t - eps). This guarantees long-run average risk <= eps + O(1/T) with no assumptions on the world model, and calibrates the decision directly instead of building prediction sets.
algorithms.how_to_adapt_to_our_problem: Decision family: the greedy plan core.plan(field, w, lambda_t, sigma). Two time scales. (1) Across operations: a sequence of fields/days in a fixed order. Use the CitrusFarm block/day order and the simulated drift scenario (fig9, moisture or RTK-scale drift). L_t = 1{missed area>0}, or the missed fraction for a risk version (comparable to CE-R). (2) Within a field, pass by pass: L_t = 1{gap between passes t-1 and t}, with target eps/(K+1) per pair, updating the erosion for the next pass (needs core.simulate_sequential as in the online-CP entry). Compare against our ACI variant, CE-U static, and CE-A. Metrics: running P(no miss), overlap, regret, and worst-window miss rate. Tune eta on training fields only. Expected: matches long-run eps under drift but gives no per-operation certificate and has a transient at start-up. That is a clean contrast to CE's offline finite-sample guarantee and supports the ACI extension.

algorithms.name: Copula Conformal Prediction for multi-step series (CopulaCPTS), as joint per-pair margins
algorithms.reference: S. H. Sun, R. Yu, 'Copula Conformal Prediction for Multi-step Time Series Forecasting', ICLR 2024 (arXiv:2212.03281).
algorithms.core_idea: Calibrates per-dimension nonconformity CDFs on one split and models their dependence with an empirical copula on a second split. It picks per-dimension quantile levels so the JOINT region has finite-sample validity, giving tighter regions than Bonferroni.
algorithms.how_to_adapt_to_our_problem: Dimensions are the K+1 constraint terms of the reference plan (adjacent pairs plus two boundary terms), with s_k^(i) = sup_x (e_{k+1}^(i)-e_k^(i))/(sigma_k+sigma_{k+1}) from core.pair_scores. Split the in-field calibration runs into D1 and D2 (use n_cal=200-300; otherwise pool terms by slope bin). On D1, fit the empirical CDFs F_k. On D2, find the common copula level u* such that the fraction of runs with all F_k(s_k) <= u* is >= (1-eps)(1+1/n2). Margins are m_k = F_k^{-1}(u*) (sigma_k+sigma_{k+1})/2 per side, and the plan uses core.plan with sig_fn = m(y). This sits between CE-U (sup-score: one quantile, implicitly exploiting dependence) and CE-pair (Bonferroni), and produces pass-specific margins, i.e. a genuinely different operating point. Expected: tighter than CE-pair, close to CE-U, with larger variance at small n. That quantifies the cost/benefit of CE's sup-score aggregation.

algorithms.name: Optimized-weight joint CP regions via (mixed-integer) linear complementarity programming
algorithms.reference: M. Cleaveland, I. Lee, G. J. Pappas, L. Lindemann, 'Conformal Prediction Regions for Time Series Using Linear Complementarity Programming', AAAI 2024, 38(19):20984-20992 (arXiv:2304.01075).
algorithms.category: joint conformal prediction with learned score normalization
algorithms.core_idea: Uses the score R = max_t alpha_t * R_t over all steps, which avoids a union bound. The weights alpha_t are chosen on an extra calibration set to minimize the resulting region size, formulated as a MILCP and relaxed to an LCP with the same optimum. Standard CP is then applied on a second calibration set.
algorithms.how_to_adapt_to_our_problem: Our score already has this max-of-weighted form with alpha_k = 1/(sigma_k+sigma_{k+1}), but CE-A fixes sigma from DEM physics and gave no gain. LCP is the principled data-driven alternative. Parameterize alpha(f_k) = 1/sigma_theta(f_k) by pair features f_k (mean side slope of both passes, slope sign relative to travel direction, chord length) with a few parameters theta. Stage 1 (D1): choose theta to minimize total erosion sum_k q(theta) sigma_theta(f_k) = overlap, where q(theta) is the empirical (1-eps) quantile of max_k alpha_k s_k. Solve as a MILP with quantile binaries (same machinery as CPP-MIP) or by grid search over 2-3 parameters. Stage 2 (D2): ordinary split-CP quantile, then core.plan. Train theta across training fields (cross-field) or in-field. Expected: if any heteroscedasticity is exploitable, LCP finds it and beats CE-U on overlap at equal validity. If not, that is evidence the CE-U/CE-A tie is a property of the data, which can be reported honestly.

algorithms.name: Online constraint-tightening learned by GP binary regression
algorithms.reference: A. Capone, T. Brüdigam, S. Hirche, 'Online Constraint Tightening in Stochastic Model Predictive Control: A Regression Approach', IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control 70(2):736-750, 2025 (arXiv:2310.02942).
algorithms.category: learning-based constraint tightening for chance constraints
algorithms.core_idea: Treats the choice of the constraint-tightening parameter as binary regression. A GP model for binary outcomes (constraint violated or not) is learned in closed loop, and the smallest tightening that meets the chance constraint is selected. This needs no exact plant model or disturbance distribution, and the paper reports tight chance-constraint satisfaction with lower cost than other SMPC tightening methods.
algorithms.how_to_adapt_to_our_problem: Tightening parameter: the erosion multiplier lambda, or lambda per field class. Each executed operation (training fields first, then the online sequence) gives input z_i = (lambda_i, field features: mean side slope, slope std, area, K, controller) and label y_i = 1{missed area>0}. Fit a GP classifier with probit/logistic link (sklearn GaussianProcessClassifier or GPyTorch variational GP). For a new field, set lambda* = min{lambda : upper-confidence p_hat(miss | lambda, features) <= eps}, using a 1-D line search on a lambda grid. Exploration: start from the slope rule and spread lambda_i over [0.5, 2]x the current estimate during training. Evaluate cross-field (exp_cross2 splits) and in the online/drift setting against CE-U, CE-A, weighted CP and ACI. Same metrics, plus the number of operations needed before validity. Expected: competitive overlap once trained, but needs hundreds of labeled operations and has no finite-sample guarantee. That contrasts with CE's 100 runs and finite-sample certificate.

notes:
The user is right on both points: a Q1 reviewer will reject a paper whose comparison is only different scalar margin rules on one planner, and whose main figure is a cluster of dots at 0 and 0.9. I found 10 published algorithms that can be run as head-to-head competitors on the same fields, simulator and metrics. They are listed above, best candidates first.

PRIORITIES
- Must-have, with code: CPP (SAIDS-Lab repo; one solver also gives the full-vector scenario approach 'SA', sample average approximation 'SAA', a KL-robust version for shift, and joint 'Max'/'Union' constraints), the GP cautious tube (befelix/safe-exploration, l4acados), and Conformal Decision Theory (Jordylek/conformal-decision).
- Must-have, coverage-specific but no code: Paull et al. ICRA 2014 / IJRR 2018, Schirmer et al. ICRA 2019, and IRIS-U^2 (Alpert et al., TRO 2025). These are the uncertainty-aware coverage planners a coverage-planning reviewer will ask about. Each needs roughly 150-300 lines of numpy.
- Strongly recommended: pass-by-pass online conformal replanning (Dixit/Lindemann/Stamouli). A real RTK tractor logs its previous pass, so reviewers will ask why that feedback is not used.

SCIENTIFIC FRAMING THESE COMPETITORS SUPPORT
1. Full-vector optimizers (CPP-MIP, scenario over all per-pass margins) choose K free margins from the same 100 runs. Either they lose validity (CPP without a data split) or they need about 10x more runs (scenario a-priori bound, d=K). CE avoids both by fixing a 1-D family before seeing the data. Make 'certified risk vs number of calibration runs' a figure.
2. Model-based planners (Paull/Schirmer belief space, IRIS-U^2 with a nominal model, GP cautious tube) are miscalibrated under heavy-tailed RTK and run-correlated slip. CE is model-free.
3. Online methods (CDT, ACI-MPC, Capone GP tightening) control only long-run risk and have a start-up transient. CE gives a per-operation finite-sample certificate.
4. CE as a wrapper: using sigma_GP or LCP-learned weights inside CE is the most promising way to finally get a CE-A gain over CE-U. If no learner beats CE-U, the paper can state honestly that the pass-to-pass error on these fields shows no exploitable heteroscedasticity.

FIGURE FIXES
- Sweep each method's own knob (target eps from 0.02 to 0.30) and plot realized P(no miss) against overlap as curves, not single points.
- Add a calibration plot of realized against nominal miss rate with the diagonal, plus an oracle frontier (best fixed lambda per field on test runs, and the IRIS-U^2 oracle).
- Show per-field violins, not just means.
- Move the baselines stuck at P=0 to a table or inset.
- Include a hard regime with strong slope heterogeneity, where CE-A versus CE-U and the learned-sigma variants can separate.

OTHER RELEVANT WORK
- Joint-in-time CP control of linear systems: Vlahakis, Lindemann, Sopasakis, Dimarogonas, IEEE L-CSS 8:2835-2840, 2024 (arXiv:2411.19132), and Vogel et al., arXiv:2512.10738 (2025; full author list unverified). Possible extension: choose the controller gains together with the CP margin.
- Scenario-based probabilistic reachable sets: Hewing & Zeilinger, IEEE L-CSS 4(2):450-455, 2020. In our setting this reduces to a scenario approach on the score.
- Finite-sample moment-based Gaussian chance constraints: Lefkopoulos & Kamgarpour, Automatica 2021, DOI 10.1016/j.automatica.2021.109754. A cheap upgrade of the 'Gaussian chance constr.' baseline.
- Robust CP for STL monitoring under f-divergence shift: Zhao, Hoxha, Fainekos, Deshmukh, Lindemann, arXiv:2311.09482 (venue unverified); code at github.com/SAIDS-Lab/Robust-Conformal-Prediction-for-STL-Runtime-Verification-under-Distribution-Shift. Relevant to the 3/10 leave-one-block/day-out failures.
- Terrain-aware deterministic agricultural planner: Hameed, la Cour-Harbo, Osen, 'Side-to-side 3D coverage path planning approach for agricultural robots to minimize skip/overlap areas between swaths', 2016. Venue unverified: one search result says J. Intelligent & Robotic Systems, but volume 76 pp. 36-45 suggests Robotics and Autonomous Systems. Natural competitor to CE-A and the slope rule.
- Base-planner swap for robustness: Fields2Cover, github.com/Fields2Cover/Fields2Cover. Not uncertainty-aware.
- Data-driven distributionally robust coverage control: Boskos, Cortes, Martinez, CDC 2023. Voronoi-type sensing coverage, less applicable; content unverified.

NOVELTY CHECK
A search for 'conformal prediction coverage path planning missed area guarantee' found no prior work combining CP with a missed-area guarantee for coverage paths. That supports the novelty claim, but cite Alpert et al. and Paull et al. as the closest coverage-under-uncertainty lines.

ACCESS AND VERIFICATION
- arXiv, ar5iv and university PDF servers could not be fetched here. Details come from search-result abstracts, and from the GitHub READMEs, which I fetched through raw.githubusercontent.com.
- No code turned up in my searches for the Lindemann 2023, Dixit 2023, Stamouli 2024, Cleaveland 2024, Capone 2025, Alpert 2025, Paull and Schirmer papers.
